A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VARE/S-VARE study and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The additional page in v2 reflects reference reflow; no material comparison gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original Infinity-2B concept-erasure experiments, baseline comparisons, robustness evaluations, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including the main comparisons and appendix multi-concept and module-selection studies.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same auxiliary-token framework, filtered cross-entropy erasure loss, KL preservation loss, and combined objective. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Training prompt-pair construction and evaluated coverage remain unchanged: nudity, Imagenette objects, artistic styles, I2P/MMA/Ring-A-Bell prompts, COCO-30K, and appendix multi-concept and synonym scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains UCE, FMN, ESD-u, ESD-x, AC-M, and AC-N. Comparator membership in the qualitative comparisons and baseline adaptations in Appendix A also remain unchanged. Newly cited ActErase is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same evaluation procedures and metrics. Table 6 still specifies Infinity-2B, 50 training prompt pairs, 500 iterations, batch size 2, and the same optimization settings.

E4.justification: The loss-component and filtering-threshold ablations, adversarial robustness tests, multi-concept study, module-selection comparisons, and reversed-loss analysis are unchanged across Section 5 and Appendices C–E.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and class averages. Neither provides repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and generated-image examples are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, both versions report S-VARE's nudity Sen.=5 and CLIP=31.3 in Table 1, and Ring-A-Bell ASR=7.4% in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(16), including the VAR/BSQ definitions, proposed objectives, and Appendix A's baseline formulations, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same novelty and surgical-erasure claims, including 97% sensitive-concept erasure with less than 2% CLIP-score degradation.

C2.justification: Explanations of error accumulation, over-optimization, and preservation remain unchanged, as do qualifications concerning style detection, diffusion-derived adversarial prompts, and multi-concept degradation. No substantive limitation or interpretation is added.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly states that code is available and supplies a S-VARE GitHub address. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and prompt-generation instructions are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: v2 adds ActErase by Sun et al. (2026) to the introduction's discussion of neuron pruning and to the bibliography. The remaining cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a code-access sentence, funding acknowledgements, and conference-status header text, and joins the contributions lead-in to its preceding paragraph. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an ICLR 2026 running header and reflows the opening text and references, shifting the appendices by one page. All thirteen figures and eight tables retain their designs, captions, and content.

improvement.justification: The new code-access address provides implementation-resource information absent from v1, and the added citation modestly updates literature coverage. Methods, experimental evidence, and appendices are unchanged, so the gain is limited to documentation and discoverability; the linked code itself cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
